notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market B2B SaaS: customer experience/productivity focus. Building an in-product chat agent and support assistant that can call internal tools (calendar, tickets, billing) and stream responses into their web app.
- Evaluating Hosted API first (fast onboarding) with plan to move to Dedicated if throughput/latency and compliance needs require it.

Recent timeline / touchpoints:
- 2025-11-12: inbound demo request from Head of Product (initial qualification). AE Jordan + SE Priya on call.
- 2025-12-02: architecture workshop (Priya) — discussed KV caching, streaming, and tool calling auth patterns. Action: provide sample call-outs and latency expectations.
- 2026-01-14: discovery call (Fireflies FF-20260114-CL-Discovery). CTO quote: "Need reliable streaming <150ms p50 for first token to client in NA/EU; p95 target <350ms."
- 2026-02-02: POC kickoff (2-week hosted API POC). Fireflies FF-20260202-POC-kickoff. POC scope doc in Drive.
- 2026-02-07 to 2026-02-21: running synthetic traffic from NA and EU regions; testing streaming, function/tool calling, and fallbacks to smaller model variants.
- 2026-02-25: interim POC sync — SE notes: streaming works but EU tail latency spikes when NA region fallback engaged; need smart routing rule examples and fallback policies.

POC objectives & acceptance criteria:
- Demonstrate streaming token latency: p50 <= 150ms (NA), p95 <= 350ms (NA); EU targets similar when routed to EU region; if routed cross-region, explain tradeoffs.
- Tool calling: authenticated secure calls to internal ticketing + calendar (OAuth flow demo). Verify no sensitive tokens in logs.
- Routing & fallback: show policy that prioritizes region then cost tier, with automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and graceful degradation for tool calls.
- Observability: dashboard with per-route latency, token cost, and KV cache hit-rate.

POC early findings (SE notes):
- Hosted API streaming meets p50 in NA under synthetic load, but EU demo traffic sees p95 spikes (~420-550ms) when fallback to NA occurs.
- KV cache reduced prompt token counts by ~18% in chat flows.
- Tool-calling auth pattern works using short-lived keys + Redwood routing; need confirmation on audit log retention and KMS integration for Dedicated.

Commercial / procurement convo:
- Interested in price compare: hosted per-token vs. monthly reserved lanes on Dedicated. Finance asked for 12/24-month committed pricing scenarios.
- Wants a clear path to Dedicated with predictable QoS and burst capacity for product launches.

Security / compliance notes:
- SOC2 required; SSO (SAML) needed for admin console.
- Data residency: prefer EU data-stay-in-EU for EU customers; need language in contract for routing policy.
- Request: sample security FAQ + SOC2 / pen-test attestation in Drive link above.

Quotes & direct feedback:
- Customer PM: "We like Redwood's streaming defaults and routing ideas — but we can't risk EU users getting NA latency on launch. Show us per-region SLOs + automated route rules."
- CTO: "If you can lock p95 in EU for streaming (or explain planned mitigation), we have a green light to move to pricing and Dedicated evaluation."

Next steps (short):
- SE to run targeted EU-only POC run next week (simulate EU-only endpoint + EU region routing).
- Redwood product to share example smart-routing policies + default fallback behavior doc.
- AE to issue a pre-proposal pricing matrix for hosted vs. Dedicated (with burst lanes) by 2026-03-10.
- Customer to complete internal security questionnaire (in Drive).
